passages.text: Earnestly pursue love and eagerly desire spiritual gifts, especially the gift of prophecy.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
He tells them to pursue love.
He tells them to desire spiritual gifts.
He says they should especially desire the gift of prophecy.
passages.original: Διώκετε τὴν ἀγάπην ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ πνευματικά μᾶλλον δὲ ἵνα προφητεύητε

passages.text: For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God. Indeed, no one understands him; he utters mysteries in the Spirit.
passages.sermon:
A person who speaks in a tongue speaks to God.
He does not speak to people.
No one understands him.
He speaks mysteries by the Spirit.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ οὐκ ἀνθρώποις λαλεῖ ἀλλὰ Θεῷ οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἀκούει πνεύματι δὲ λαλεῖ μυστήρια

passages.text: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, encouragement, and comfort.
passages.sermon:
The person who prophesies speaks to people.
He builds them up.
He encourages them.
He gives them comfort.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ προφητεύων ἀνθρώποις λαλεῖ οἰκοδομὴν καὶ παράκλησιν καὶ παραμυθίαν

passages.text: The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul explains spiritual gifts.
A person who speaks in a tongue builds up himself.
A person who prophesies builds up the church.
passages.original: ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ ἑαυτὸν οἰκοδομεῖ ὁ δὲ προφητεύων ἐκκλησίαν οἰκοδομεῖ

passages.text: I wish that all of you could speak in tongues, but I would rather have you prophesy. He who prophesies is greater than one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets so that the church may be edified.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle and teacher of the church.
\r\nPaul wishes that all believers could speak in tongues.
\r\nPaul prefers that believers prophesy.
\r\nA person who prophesies is greater than a person who speaks in tongues.
\r\nA person who speaks in tongues is not greater unless he interprets.
\r\nIf he interprets, the church receives edification.
passages.original: Θέλω δὲ πάντας ὑμᾶς λαλεῖν γλώσσαις μᾶλλον δὲ ἵνα προφητεύητε μείζων δὲ ὁ προφητεύων ἢ ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσαις ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ διερμηνεύῃ ἵνα ἡ ἐκκλησία οἰκοδομὴν λάβῃ

passages.text: Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you, unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church.
Paul calls the people "brothers."
Paul says, "If I come to you and speak in tongues, I do not help you."
Paul says, "I only help you if I bring you revelation."
Paul says, "I only help you if I bring you knowledge."
Paul says, "I only help you if I bring you prophecy."
Paul says, "I only help you if I bring you teaching."
passages.original: Νῦν δέ ἀδελφοί ἐὰν ἔλθω πρὸς ὑμᾶς γλώσσαις λαλῶν τί ὑμᾶς ὠφελήσω ἐὰν μὴ ὑμῖν λαλήσω ἢ ἐν ἀποκαλύψει ἢ ἐν γνώσει ἢ ἐν προφητείᾳ ἢ ἐν διδαχῇ

passages.text: Even in the case of lifeless instruments, such as the flute or harp, how will anyone recognize the tune they are playing unless the notes are distinct?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
Paul uses lifeless instruments as an example.
A flute and a harp are lifeless instruments.
These instruments make sounds.
If the notes are not clear, no one can recognize the tune.
People cannot know what is being played if the notes are not distinct.
Distinct notes are necessary to recognize the music.
passages.original: ὅμως τὰ ἄψυχα φωνὴν διδόντα εἴτε αὐλὸς εἴτε κιθάρα ἐὰν διαστολὴν τοῖς φθόγγοις μὴ δῷ πῶς γνωσθήσεται τὸ αὐλούμενον ἢ τὸ κιθαριζόμενον

passages.text: Again, if the trumpet sounds a muffled call, who will prepare for battle?
passages.sermon:
A trumpet is a musical instrument.
A trumpet gives a signal with its sound.
If the trumpet gives an unclear sound, people cannot understand the signal.
If the sound is not clear, no one will get ready for battle.
passages.original: Καὶ γὰρ ἐὰν ἄδηλον σάλπιγξ φωνὴν δῷ τίς παρασκευάσεται εἰς πόλεμον

passages.text: So it is with you. Unless you speak intelligible words with your tongue, how will anyone know what you are saying? You will just be speaking into the air.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
He addresses Christians who desire spiritual gifts.
He says, "You must speak clear words with your tongue."
If you do not speak clear words, people will not understand you.
No one will know what you are saying.
You will only be speaking into the air.
passages.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς διὰ τῆς γλώσσης ἐὰν μὴ εὔσημον λόγον δῶτε πῶς γνωσθήσεται τὸ λαλούμενον ἔσεσθε γὰρ εἰς ἀέρα λαλοῦντες

passages.text: Assuredly, there are many different languages in the world, yet none of them is without meaning.
passages.sermon: There are many kinds of languages in the world.\r\nEach language has meaning.\r\nNo language is without meaning.
passages.original: Τοσαῦτα εἰ τύχοι γένη φωνῶν εἰσιν ἐν κόσμῳ καὶ οὐδὲν ἄφωνον

passages.text: If, then, I do not know the meaning of someone’s language, I am a foreigner to the speaker, and he is a foreigner to me.
passages.sermon:
If I do not know the meaning of a person's language,
I become a foreigner to that person.
That person also becomes a foreigner to me.
We cannot understand each other.
We are like strangers to one another.
passages.original: ἐὰν οὖν μὴ εἰδῶ τὴν δύναμιν τῆς φωνῆς ἔσομαι τῷ λαλοῦντι βάρβαρος καὶ ὁ λαλῶν ἐν ἐμοὶ βάρβαρος

passages.text: It is the same with you. Since you are eager to have spiritual gifts, strive to excel in gifts that build up the church.
passages.sermon:
You are eager to have spiritual gifts.
You want to receive these gifts.
You belong to the church.
You should try to excel in gifts that build up the church.
You should seek gifts that help the church grow strong.
passages.original: Οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐπεὶ ζηλωταί ἐστε πνευμάτων πρὸς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τῆς ἐκκλησίας ζητεῖτε ἵνα περισσεύητε

passages.text: Therefore, the one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.
passages.sermon:
A person may speak in a tongue.
A tongue is a language unknown to others.
This person should pray.
He should pray to interpret what he says.
He should ask God to help him explain the meaning.
This helps others understand his words.
passages.original: Διὸ ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ προσευχέσθω ἵνα διερμηνεύῃ

passages.text: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in Corinth.
\r\nHe explains what happens when he prays in a tongue.
\r\nIf I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays.
\r\nBut my mind does not produce fruit.
\r\nMy mind does not understand or benefit.
passages.original: ἐὰν γὰρ προσεύχωμαι γλώσσῃ τὸ πνεῦμά μου προσεύχεται ὁ δὲ νοῦς μου ἄκαρπός ἐστιν

passages.text: What then shall I do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my mind.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church about prayer and worship.
\r\nPaul asks, "What should I do?"
\r\nPaul says, "I will pray with my spirit."
\r\nPaul also says, "I will pray with my mind."
\r\nPaul says, "I will sing with my spirit."
\r\nPaul also says, "I will sing with my mind."
passages.original: Τί οὖν ἐστιν προσεύξομαι τῷ πνεύματι προσεύξομαι δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ ψαλῶ τῷ πνεύματι ψαλῶ δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ

passages.text: Otherwise, if you speak a blessing in spirit, how can someone who is uninstructed say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church about spiritual gifts and public worship.
Paul addresses the use of speaking in tongues.
If you bless or give thanks in the spirit, you speak in a language others do not understand.
An uninstructed person is someone who does not understand the language you use.
If you speak a blessing in the spirit, the uninstructed person cannot understand your words.
The uninstructed person cannot say “Amen” to your thanksgiving.
He cannot agree with your prayer because he does not know what you are saying.
passages.original: ἐπεὶ ἐὰν εὐλογῇς ἐν πνεύματι ὁ ἀναπληρῶν τὸν τόπον τοῦ ἰδιώτου πῶς ἐρεῖ τὸ Ἀμήν ἐπὶ τῇ σῇ εὐχαριστίᾳ ἐπειδὴ τί λέγεις οὐκ οἶδεν

passages.text: You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other one is not edified.
passages.sermon: You may give thanks well.\r\nAnother person does not receive help.\r\nThe other person is not built up.
passages.original: σὺ μὲν γὰρ καλῶς εὐχαριστεῖς ἀλλ’ ὁ ἕτερος οὐκ οἰκοδομεῖται

passages.text: I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nPaul thanks God.
\r\nPaul speaks in tongues.
\r\nPaul speaks in tongues more than all of you.
passages.original: Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ Θεῷ πάντων ὑμῶν μᾶλλον γλώσσαις λαλῶ

passages.text: But in the church, I would rather speak five coherent words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church.
Paul values clear teaching.
Paul wants to help others understand.
Paul prefers to speak five clear words.
Paul uses his mind to speak these words.
Paul wants to instruct others with these words.
Paul does not prefer to speak many words in a tongue.
Paul says ten thousand words in a tongue are less helpful.
Paul chooses what builds up the church.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ θέλω πέντε λόγους τῷ νοΐ μου λαλῆσαι ἵνα καὶ ἄλλους κατηχήσω ἢ μυρίους λόγους ἐν γλώσσῃ

passages.text: Brothers, stop thinking like children. In regard to evil be infants, but in your thinking be mature.
passages.sermon: Brothers, do not think like children.\r\nBe innocent like infants when it comes to evil.\r\nBe mature in your thinking.
passages.original: Ἀδελφοί μὴ παιδία γίνεσθε ταῖς φρεσίν ἀλλὰ τῇ κακίᾳ νηπιάζετε ταῖς δὲ φρεσὶν τέλειοι γίνεσθε

passages.text: It is written in the Law: “By strange tongues and foreign lips I will speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to Me, says the Lord.”
passages.sermon:
The Law contains a message from God.
God says, “I will speak to this people.”
I will use strange tongues.
I will use foreign lips.
Even then, they will not listen to Me.
The Lord says this.
passages.original: ἐν τῷ νόμῳ γέγραπται ὅτι Ἐν ἑτερογλώσσοις καὶ ἐν χείλεσιν ἑτέρων λαλήσω τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ καὶ οὐδ’ οὕτως εἰσακούσονταί μου λέγει Κύριος

passages.text: Tongues, then, are a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers. Prophecy, however, is for believers, not for unbelievers.
passages.sermon:
Tongues are a sign.
Tongues are not for believers.
Tongues are for unbelievers.
Prophecy is not for unbelievers.
Prophecy is for believers.
passages.original: Ὥστε αἱ γλῶσσαι εἰς σημεῖόν εἰσιν οὐ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἀπίστοις ἡ δὲ προφητεία οὐ τοῖς ἀπίστοις ἀλλὰ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν

passages.text: So if the whole church comes together and everyone speaks in tongues, and some who are uninstructed or some unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are out of your minds?
passages.sermon:
The church is a group of believers in Jesus Christ.
Sometimes the whole church gathers in one place.
Everyone in the church may speak in tongues.
Uninstructed people may enter the gathering.
Unbelievers may also enter the gathering.
These visitors do not understand the language spoken.
They hear everyone speaking in tongues.
They will say that the church members are out of their minds.
passages.original: Ἐὰν οὖν συνέλθῃ ἡ ἐκκλησία ὅλη ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ πάντες λαλῶσιν γλώσσαις εἰσέλθωσιν δὲ ἰδιῶται ἢ ἄπιστοι οὐκ ἐροῦσιν ὅτι μαίνεσθε

passages.text: But if an unbeliever or uninstructed person comes in while everyone is prophesying, he will be convicted and called to account by all, and the secrets of his heart will be made known. So he will fall facedown and worship God, proclaiming, “God is truly among you!”
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church.
He describes what happens when the church prophesies.
An unbeliever or an uninstructed person may enter the gathering.
The believers prophesy together.
The unbeliever hears the words.
He is convicted by all.
He is called to account by all.
The secrets of his heart become known.
He realizes his hidden thoughts are revealed.
He falls facedown.
He worships God.
He says, “God is truly among you.”
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ πάντες προφητεύωσιν εἰσέλθῃ δέ τις ἄπιστος ἢ ἰδιώτης ἐλέγχεται ὑπὸ πάντων ἀνακρίνεται ὑπὸ πάντων τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ φανερὰ γίνεται καὶ οὕτως πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον προσκυνήσει τῷ Θεῷ ἀπαγγέλλων ὅτι Ὄντως ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστιν

passages.text: What then shall we say, brothers? When you come together, everyone has a psalm or a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. All of these must be done to build up the church.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church.
He calls the believers brothers.
He describes what happens when the church gathers.
Each person brings something.
One has a psalm.
One has a teaching.
One has a revelation.
One has a tongue.
One has an interpretation.
All these things must help build up the church.
passages.original: Τί οὖν ἐστιν ἀδελφοί ὅταν συνέρχησθε ἕκαστος ψαλμὸν ἔχει διδαχὴν ἔχει ἀποκάλυψιν ἔχει γλῶσσαν ἔχει ἑρμηνείαν ἔχει πάντα πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν γινέσθω

passages.text: If anyone speaks in a tongue, two, or at most three, should speak in turn, and someone must interpret.
passages.sermon:
Paul gives instructions for church gatherings.
He addresses the use of speaking in tongues.
If anyone speaks in a tongue, only two or three people should speak.
They must speak one at a time.
Someone must interpret what is said.
passages.original: Εἴτε γλώσσῃ τις λαλεῖ κατὰ δύο ἢ τὸ πλεῖστον τρεῖς καὶ ἀνὰ μέρος καὶ εἷς διερμηνευέτω

passages.text: But if there is no interpreter, he should remain silent in the church and speak only to himself and God.
passages.sermon: If there is no interpreter, the person must stay silent in the church.\r\nHe may speak only to himself and to God.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ διερμηνευτής σιγάτω ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἑαυτῷ δὲ λαλείτω καὶ τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should weigh carefully what is said.
passages.sermon:
Prophets are people who speak messages from God.
Two prophets should speak.
Or three prophets should speak.
Other people must listen.
The others must judge what the prophets say.
The others must think carefully about the message.
passages.original: Προφῆται δὲ δύο ἢ τρεῖς λαλείτωσαν καὶ οἱ ἄλλοι διακρινέτωσαν

passages.text: And if a revelation comes to someone who is seated, the first speaker should stop.
passages.sermon: A revelation may come to a person who is sitting.\r\nIf this happens, the first speaker must stop speaking.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ ἄλλῳ ἀποκαλυφθῇ καθημένῳ ὁ πρῶτος σιγάτω

passages.text: For you can all prophesy in turn so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church.
He addresses believers who have the gift of prophecy.
Each person with this gift can speak one at a time.
All believers can take turns to prophesy.
This allows everyone to learn.
This allows everyone to receive encouragement.
passages.original: δύνασθε γὰρ καθ’ ἕνα πάντες προφητεύειν ἵνα πάντες μανθάνωσιν καὶ πάντες παρακαλῶνται

passages.text: The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
passages.sermon:
Prophets have control over their own spirits.
Prophets can choose when and how to speak.
Prophets do not lose self-control when they prophesy.
Prophets must act with order and discipline.
passages.original: καὶ πνεύματα προφητῶν προφήταις ὑποτάσσεται

passages.text: For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace—as in all the churches of the saints.
passages.sermon:
God is not a God of disorder.
God is a God of peace.
God brings peace in all the churches of the saints.
God acts the same way in every church of His holy people.
passages.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀκαταστασίας ὁ Θεὸς ἀλλὰ εἰρήνης Ὡς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῶν ἁγίων

passages.text: Women are to be silent in the churches. They are not permitted to speak, but must be in submission, as the law says.
passages.sermon:
Paul addresses the churches of the saints.
He gives instructions for order in worship.
God is a God of peace, not disorder.
Women must be silent in the churches.
Women are not allowed to speak in the churches.
Women must be in submission.
The law also commands women to be in submission.
passages.original: αἱ γυναῖκες ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις σιγάτωσαν οὐ γὰρ ἐπιτρέπεται αὐταῖς λαλεῖν ἀλλὰ ὑποτασσέσθωσαν καθὼς καὶ ὁ νόμος λέγει

passages.text: If they wish to inquire about something, they are to ask their own husbands at home; for it is dishonorable for a woman to speak in the church.
passages.sermon:
Paul addresses women in the church.
He says women must not speak in the church.
If women want to learn something, they must ask their own husbands at home.
It is shameful for a woman to speak in the church.
passages.original: εἰ δέ τι μαθεῖν θέλουσιν ἐν οἴκῳ τοὺς ἰδίους ἄνδρας ἐπερωτάτωσαν αἰσχρὸν γάρ ἐστιν γυναικὶ λαλεῖν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ

passages.text: Did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?
passages.sermon:
Paul addresses the church in Corinth.
Paul asks if the word of God began with them.
Paul asks if the word of God came only to them.
Paul challenges their authority to set rules apart from God’s word.
passages.original: Ἢ ἀφ’ ὑμῶν ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐξῆλθεν ἢ εἰς ὑμᾶς μόνους κατήντησεν

passages.text: If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual person, let him acknowledge that what I am writing you is the Lord’s command.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church in Corinth.
Paul gave instructions about order in worship.
If anyone thinks he is a prophet, he must listen.
If anyone thinks he is a spiritual person, he must listen.
He must recognize what I write to you.
What I write is a command from the Lord.
passages.original: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ προφήτης εἶναι ἢ πνευματικός ἐπιγινωσκέτω ἃ γράφω ὑμῖν ὅτι Κυρίου ἐστὶν ἐντολή

passages.text: But if anyone ignores this, he himself will be ignored.
passages.sermon: If anyone ignores this command from the Lord, God will ignore that person.
passages.original: εἰ δέ τις ἀγνοεῖ ἀγνοεῖται

passages.text: So, my brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the believers in Corinth.
Paul calls them brothers.
Paul urges them to desire to prophesy.
Paul tells them to be eager to prophesy.
Paul commands them not to forbid speaking in tongues.
passages.original: Ὥστε ἀδελφοί μου ζηλοῦτε τὸ προφητεύειν καὶ τὸ λαλεῖν μὴ κωλύετε γλώσσαις

passages.text: But everything must be done in a proper and orderly manner.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
He gives instructions for worship.
He says, “Do everything properly.”
He says, “Do everything in an orderly way.”
passages.original: πάντα δὲ εὐσχημόνως καὶ κατὰ τάξιν γινέσθω
